name: Elam
overview: Elam was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically noted as the fifth-born son of Meshelemiah, also known as Shallum. His identity is primarily established through his genealogical placement within the Levitical lineage, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 26:3. Beyond this, there are no additional notes or details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Elam is a proper name meaning 'highland.' It is not indicated that this name was given by God, but it is preserved in Scripture as part of the Levitical genealogy in 1 Chronicles 26:3. The meaning of his name reflects a geographical term rather than a theological title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elam as the son of Shallum (Meshelemiah), confirming his place within a Levitical family line. No other family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection in 1 Chronicles 26:3.
scriptureSignificance: Elam's significance lies in his inclusion in the detailed genealogical records of the tribe of Levi, emphasizing the importance of Levitical families in the organization and service of Israel's worship. Being a descendant of Meshelemiah situates him within the priestly or Levitical divisions that played crucial roles in temple duties. Though not highlighted for specific deeds, Elam represents the continuity of God's covenant people through faithful lineage.
